articles.title: Start here
articles.description: Understand what the console controls and the order in which to use it.

blocks.text: The Research Console is the operating view over the QuantSilico Everesteer engine. The command-line engine remains the critical path; the dashboard reads the same filesystem evidence and backend state so that you can see what is happening without reconstructing it from logs.

It is normal for Event Control to show **NOT CONNECTED**, for leaderboard values
to be blank and for event capabilities to be unknown.
Do not populate those fields manually.

Use synthetic rehearsal to prove that the local machinery works without
pretending that a live event exists.
Start by inspecting the platform rather than training immediately.
Then capture the event state that subsequent actions will be tied to.

The event/API and organiser instructions are authoritative for event mechanics.
Do not make an old README override the live event.
The project has three submission states.

blocks.name: DRY_RUN
blocks.text: The submission pipeline can validate, package and record evidence without uploading predictions to Everesteer. This is the safe default.

blocks.name: ARMED
blocks.text: Real Everesteer uploads are permitted after explicit human action and still remain subject to event, lane, quota, ID and artefact checks.
Autopilot must never arm submissions by itself.
Use **Overview** to understand the current operating stage.
Use **Event Control** to verify platform state.
Use **Data Lab** before trusting a newly downloaded split.
Use **Round Room**, **Submission** and **Leaderboard** during live rounds.

Use **Compute & Jobs** when you need to know whether an experiment will finish
in useful time.

articles.title: Research loop
articles.description: How an idea becomes evidence, a frontier candidate, a champion or a retired branch.

blocks.text: Research is not a sequence of models to try once. It is a measured loop that spends small amounts of compute first, retains useful evidence and increases budget only when a candidate still has something to teach us.
What the race is trying to answer
Champion, frontier and ensemble are different
R0 asks whether the candidate works at all.
R1 asks whether there is enough signal to spend more compute.
R2 asks whether the evidence remains useful under more complete validation.

R3 is for candidates that may become an operational champion or a serious
ensemble member.
A weak score is not automatically an integrity failure.
A candidate must stop when the evidence is invalid rather than merely weak.

Valid candidates can be compared using whatever evidence is actually available,
including:
No single soft metric is a universal veto.

blocks.name: Champion
blocks.text: The operational default candidate if a prediction had to be produced now.

blocks.name: Frontier
blocks.text: The set of candidates that remain interesting because no other candidate is clearly better on every relevant trade-off.

blocks.name: Ensemble
blocks.text: A constructed candidate combining multiple prediction streams.

A model can therefore remain valuable even when it does not beat the champion
alone.

articles.title: Data validation
articles.description: Audit, fingerprint and split identity before any modelling or submit.

blocks.text: A dataset is not trusted because it arrived. It is trusted after structural audit and a content fingerprint that later inference and submission can match.

`qseh data audit` runs `audit_dataset` on a Parquet or CSV file. It records row
and column counts, ID and exped columns, target availability, duplicate IDs,
missingness and a schema SHA-256.

Integrity is `pass`, `warn` or `fail`. A hard failure is an integrity stop, not
a weak research score.

`qseh data fingerprint` records the file content hash and schema fingerprint.
Live-round inference should reuse a prediction artefact only when the live split
fingerprint is unchanged.

Train, validation/practice and live splits are different files. Submission
guard checks the split fingerprint against the event snapshot so a train file
cannot be uploaded as live.

Synthetic fixtures generated with `QSEH_SYNTHETIC=1` remain labelled
`SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE` and must not be treated as official event data.
Do not spend compute on a split whose audit integrity is fail.

articles.title: Model lifecycle
articles.description: How a candidate is fit, stored, loaded for inference and retired.

blocks.text: Models enter the system through the shared research interface. Submission consumes a normal candidate; there is no model-specific upload path.

`ExperimentRunner` reads YAML, fits through `create_model`, writes OOF
predictions, fold metrics, resource measurements and an immutable run manifest
under `runs/experiments/<run_id>/`. Failed runs keep their evidence.

Factories currently registered include ridge, random_forest, extra_trees,
xgboost, lgbm, reference_lgbm and shallow_mlp.

`ModelRegistry` stores the fitted object and training data hash when provided.
A later live infer must load that artefact rather than refitting from memory.

Record parent candidate and config delta when an operator changes
regularisation, features, recency, seed or ensemble membership. Experiments
that cannot explain what changed are not useful under a live clock.

Round-room inference uses the champion or an approved ensemble. Submission
guard then checks event, lane, IDs, artefacts and quota. Do not add
model-specific submission code.

articles.title: Live round workflow
articles.description: What happens from a newly opened round to a recorded result.

blocks.text: Use this flow once Everesteer exposes a live round. The objective is to move from a verified live split to a recorded submission without rebuilding the research system while the clock is running.

blocks.name: Time remaining
blocks.text: The authoritative estimate of how long the current round remains open.

blocks.name: Split fingerprint
blocks.text: The content identity of the live dataset currently being used for inference.

blocks.name: Inference ETA
blocks.text: Whether the selected candidate will finish early enough to be useful.

blocks.name: Upload budget
blocks.text: How many external submissions remain available.
When a live result is poor

The live-round controller should detect the event state and avoid repeated work
when the dataset fingerprint is unchanged.

The same round must not accidentally produce duplicate external uploads after a
restart.
Do not immediately rewrite the model stack.

One noisy external round is evidence, not a command to discard all prior local
validation.
Do not start an architectural refactor while a live round is closing.

articles.title: Submission path
articles.description: How a research candidate becomes a validated practice or live upload.

blocks.text: Submission is an external side effect. Every upload must remain attributable to a candidate, event snapshot, dataset fingerprint, prediction artefact and model artefact.
The submission guard checks, where applicable:
A red integrity failure blocks the external action.
Use DRY_RUN while validating the system.
Real uploads require explicit human intent.
Do not arm until account, event and snapshot identity have been verified.
Neither rehearsal nor autopilot may automatically transition the system to ARMED.
A restart must not submit the same action twice.

Submission history therefore records enough context to identify an equivalent
event/round/split/candidate/action combination.

articles.title: Event-day operator guide
articles.description: Beginning-to-end operating guide for the Everesteer competition.

blocks.text: This is the document to use when operating the system under time pressure. Commands are shown with the repository virtual-environment executable directly; PowerShell activation is not required.
The repository is designed to use:

A successful preflight proves the local machinery works. It does not prove that
live Everesteer credentials or event datasets already exist.
Do not begin by editing configuration based on assumptions. Read the event first.
This becomes the evidence anchor for later data and submission operations.
Pull validation/practice data if the event exposes it:

Use Data Lab to inspect row counts, schema, missingness, IDs and target
availability.
Do not spend the competition optimising against a scorer you do not trust.

This tests the normal path from real data through training, validation, model
artefact and prediction generation.
Once the basic path is healthy:
Use Experiments and Validation to watch evidence.

Early research should spend small budgets broadly before spending large budgets
on one family.

A practice submission is not just an attempt to score points. It purchases
external evidence.
Do not waste limited uploads on nearly identical random seeds.

Only after verifying the actual event should you explicitly arm external
uploads.
Reduce exploration as useful time disappears.
Capture evidence before shutting things down.

Do not immediately `git add -A`; event datasets, predictions and local research
evidence may intentionally remain private.

articles.title: Dashboard operations
articles.description: Start, verify, diagnose and recover the local Research Console.

blocks.text: The dashboard is an operational cockpit, not the authority for research state. The filesystem-backed engine and CLI remain usable if the browser or dashboard server fails.

This checks the Python environment, application import, frontend build, runtime
state, process state, port and health endpoint.
A returned PID by itself is not considered success.
The browser should not be opened by this command when the backend is unhealthy.

Use this after deliberate frontend changes. Do not reinstall packages casually
during a live round.
If the dashboard fails during a round
The process manager only terminates the dashboard process it owns.
Restart the UI only when doing so will not distract from the competition path.

articles.title: Developer guide
articles.description: How the Everesteer competition system is structured and how to extend it without breaking live operation.

blocks.text: This guide is for changing the system rather than operating a competition round. The central rule is to preserve evidence lineage and keep the CLI, backend and Research Console as different views over the same domain state.
The CLI and autopilot invoke the same domain concepts independently of the UI.
The dashboard must never become the only copy of competition state.
Experiment evidence lives under the run/artifact structure.

A database may index this material for fast queries, but the database must be
rebuildable from the evidence files.
Do not add model-specific submission code.
An operator changes one well-defined part of an existing candidate, for example:
Record the parent and config delta.
Do not create experiments that cannot later explain what changed.

TypeScript page DTO
→ Python/Pydantic mirror
→ domain service
→ API route
→ ApiDataSource
→ component
Do not put a field directly into React using a second ad-hoc fetch.
Unknown values remain null/unknown rather than being turned into zero.
Read-only repository/build inspection is allowed through narrow services.
Every button that mutates state must map to an allowlisted domain action.
A production button is not allowed to be decorative.
Document its path in the dashboard live-wiring matrix.

Frequently changing domains can publish logical events through the configured
SSE/WebSocket mechanism.
Do not poll every backend domain at the same interval.
Submission is a privileged external side effect.

Development and CI must remain incapable of accidentally arming external
submission.
Synthetic fixtures exist to test infrastructure without organiser data.

Synthetic evidence must remain distinguishable internally from official event
evidence.
Rehearsal must not overwrite live production research state.
Human operating knowledge stays in curated MDX.
Run the smallest relevant tests first.

Do not treat a disconnected live Everesteer event as a local code failure when
credentials have not yet been provided.
Never solve a live-round problem by performing a broad architecture cleanup.

articles.title: Glossary
articles.description: Terms used by the Research Console, CLI and generated reference.

blocks.text: Short definitions for words that appear in the operator guides and generated reference. These are operating terms, not invented scoring formulas.

blocks.name: ICIR
blocks.text: Information coefficient information ratio: a soft research metric used when comparing valid candidates. It is not a universal veto.

blocks.name: CORR20
blocks.text: An official-style score component name probed from everestapi.scoring when the SDK exposes it. Local fallbacks are labelled non-official.

blocks.name: exped
blocks.text: The time-group column used by temporal splits. Fold profiles R0–R3 allocate train/test expeds with optional embargo.

blocks.name: DRY_RUN
blocks.text: Submission pipeline may validate, package and record evidence without uploading to Everesteer. Safe default.

blocks.name: ARMED
blocks.text: Real Everesteer uploads are permitted after explicit `qseh event arm-submissions` and still pass guard checks.

blocks.name: Champion
blocks.text: The operational default candidate if a prediction had to be produced now.

blocks.name: Frontier
blocks.text: Candidates that remain interesting because no other candidate is clearly better on every relevant trade-off.

blocks.name: Ensemble
blocks.text: A constructed candidate combining multiple prediction streams.

blocks.name: QSEH_SYNTHETIC
blocks.text: Environment flag that forces synthetic fixtures instead of live dataset pulls.
